title: Autocomplete Search Box
prompt: Build the search box for a large shopping site. As the user types, show up to eight suggestions under the input, and let them pick one with the mouse, touch or keyboard.

clarify.q: Where do suggestions come from: a server endpoint, or a list we already have in the browser?
clarify.why: A server source makes this a network problem (debounce, races, caching). A local list of 50 000 items makes it a CPU problem (indexing, maybe a Web Worker).

clarify.q: Are suggestions one kind of thing, or mixed (products, categories, recent searches)?
clarify.why: Mixed results need groups with headings, a type field in the payload, and a different render per type. It also changes the ARIA markup (grouped listbox).

clarify.q: What happens on select: navigate to a page, fill the input, or call back into the parent?
clarify.why: It decides the component's events. A navigating box can render real links; a form field needs onSelect and a controlled value.

clarify.q: Which locales and input methods must work? Korean, Japanese, Chinese?
clarify.why: IME users type through composition events. Firing a request on every composed jamo sends garbage queries and flickers the list, so we must wait for compositionend.

clarify.q: Is this one widget for one page, or a reusable component for the design system?
clarify.why: A reusable component needs a generic data-source prop, render props for items, and strict accessibility, rather than a hard-coded fetch.

clarify.q: Do we show recent searches when the box is focused but empty?
clarify.why: That adds local persistence (localStorage), a privacy question (clear history), and a zero-query state that needs no network.
If the endpoint costs real money per call, debounce harder and cache more. If it is a cheap edge-cached index, we can be more eager.

functional: Show up to 8 suggestions for the current text once it has at least 1 character (2 for Latin scripts, configurable).
Highlight the part of each suggestion that matches the query.
Arrow keys move through suggestions, Enter picks the active one, Escape closes the list, and a second Escape clears the input.
With an empty focused input, show up to 5 recent searches stored on the device, each removable.
Pressing Enter with no active suggestion submits a full search to /search?q=…
Show clear loading, no-results and error states without layout jumps.
nonFunctional: Typing never lags: every keystroke echoes within one frame (16.7 ms); INP under 200 ms on a mid-range Android phone.
Suggestions appear within 500 ms of the last keystroke on slow 4G (150 ms RTT) with a warm connection.
A stale response never overwrites a newer one, and the list never shows results for text the user has already changed.
Fully usable with a keyboard and a screen reader (WAI-ARIA combobox pattern, tested with VoiceOver and NVDA).
Component JavaScript under 6 KB gzipped; no layout shift (CLS 0) when the list opens.
At most ~3 network requests per typed query on average.
outOfScope: The ranking and indexing backend (that is the separate typeahead-autocomplete problem).
Spelling correction and search-results page design.
Personalised suggestions based on account history.

assumptions: 10 M daily active users, 4 searches each per day
Average query is 8 characters; inside a word keys come ~120 ms apart, with 2–3 pauses of 300 ms or more
Slow 4G: 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps down; server responds in ~40 ms
Payload: 8 suggestions of ~140 bytes JSON each
Mid-range phone: ~4× slower CPU than a dev laptop

steps.label: Requests per query
steps.math: No debounce: 8 keys → 8 requests. Debounce 200 ms fires only at the 2–3 pauses → ~3; ~15% hit the client cache (backspace, retype) → 3 × 0.85
steps.result: ≈ 2.5 network requests per query instead of 8

steps.label: Server load
steps.math: 10 M × 4 = 40 M queries/day. 40 M × 2.5 = 100 M req/day ÷ 86 400 s ≈ 1 160/s. Without debounce: 40 M × 8 = 320 M ÷ 86 400 ≈ 3 700/s

steps.label: Payload
steps.math: 8 × 140 B ≈ 1.1 KB JSON; repeated keys gzip well

steps.label: Network time on slow 4G
steps.math: Transfer: 0.5 KB = 4 Kbit ÷ 1.6 Mbps ≈ 2.5 ms. Warm: 150 ms RTT + 40 ms server. Cold adds DNS + TCP + TLS ≈ 3 RTT = 450 ms
steps.result: ≈ 190 ms warm, ≈ 640 ms cold: latency is all round trips, not bytes

steps.label: Perceived latency
steps.math: 200 ms debounce + 190 ms network + ~5 ms render
steps.result: ≈ 400 ms after the last key: inside the 500 ms target only if the connection is warm

steps.label: Local filtering cost (if data is in the browser)
steps.math: 50 000 items × ~0.5 µs per compare on a phone ≈ 25 ms
steps.result: 25 ms > one 16.7 ms frame: needs a prefix index or a worker

steps.label: Client cache memory
steps.result: ≈ 110 KB: trivial, keep it per page session

estimates.takeaway: Latency is round trips, not bytes: a 0.5 KB payload is nothing, but a cold connection costs 450 ms. So preconnect when the input gets focus and use a short debounce. Debounce cuts server calls by about 70%. For a local data set, the risk moves to the main thread: a naive filter over 50 000 items misses the frame budget.

api.body: { label, fetchSuggestions(query, { signal }) → Promise<{ items, complete }>, minChars = 1, debounceMs = 200, maxItems = 8, renderItem?(item, { query, active }), getItemKey(item), value?, defaultValue?, placeholder? }
api.returns: Renders a labelled combobox input and a popup listbox
api.note: fetchSuggestions receives an AbortSignal so the caller's fetch can be cancelled. value/defaultValue lets the parent control the text or not.
onSelect for picking a suggestion, onSubmit for Enter with no active option. Parent decides whether to navigate.

api.body: Query normalised client-side: trimmed, lower-cased, Unicode NFKC
api.returns: 200 { q, items: [{ id, type, label, matches: [[0,3]], url, thumb? }], complete: true|false }
api.note: Top-k list, so no pagination. matches are character ranges to highlight, so the client never injects HTML. complete=true means there are no more matches than the ones sent.

api.returns: CDN and browser cache popular prefixes for 5 minutes
api.note: Safe because suggestions are not personalised. Vary: Accept-Language if locale is not in the URL.
Only the submitted query lives in the URL; typed-but-not-submitted text does not.

entities.name: ComboboxState
entities.store: Component state (useReducer or a small store)
entities.why: One reducer with explicit transitions keeps open/close, loading and keyboard state consistent. resultsFor lets us check items match the visible text.

entities.name: SuggestionCache
entities.store: In-memory LRU Map, module scope, 100 entries
entities.why: Backspace and retyping are instant. Module scope means the cache survives the input unmounting and remounting.

entities.name: RecentSearches
entities.why: Max 5 entries, newest first, de-duplicated. Read in a try/catch because storage can be blocked.

entities.name: Suggestion
entities.why: Plain text plus ranges, never pre-built HTML, so highlighting cannot become an XSS hole.

data.note: The input text is the only source of truth for the query. Everything else is derived from it or keyed by it. The cache key is the normalised query plus locale, so ' iPhone' and 'iphone' share an entry. Nothing goes in the URL until submit, because the URL should describe a result page, not a half-typed word.

hld.summary:
The component is an input plus a popup listbox. Keystrokes update query at once, so typing never waits on anything. A debouncer turns the stream of keystrokes into fetch triggers. Each trigger checks the LRU cache first. On a miss, the fetcher aborts the previous request, sends a new one with an id, and drops any response whose id is not the latest.

The listbox renders from items only when resultsFor matches the current text. A visually hidden live region announces the result count. Selection either calls onSelect or follows the item's link. The connection is warmed when the input gets focus, so the first request is not a cold one.

diagram.title: Component tree and data flow
diagram.src:
flowchart LR
  IN["SearchInput (role combobox)"] -->|keystroke| RED[Combobox reducer]
  IN -->|text after pause| DEB[Debouncer 200 ms]
  DEB --> CACHE["Prefix cache (LRU)"]
  CACHE -->|hit| RED
  CACHE -->|miss| FET["Fetcher (abort + request id)"]
  FET --> API["GET /v1/suggest"]
  API --> CDN[CDN edge cache]
  FET -->|latest response only| RED
  RED --> LB["Listbox (role listbox)"]
  RED --> LIVE[Live region]
  LB -->|select| OUT[onSelect or navigate]
  RS[Recent searches in localStorage] --> LB

flows.title: Typing 'iph' quickly
steps: Each key updates query and redraws the input in the same frame; no fetch yet.
After 200 ms with no key, the debouncer fires with 'iph'.
Cache miss: the previous controller is aborted, request id 7 goes out with a new AbortSignal.
status becomes 'loading', but the old list stays visible (dimmed) to avoid flicker.
Response id 7 arrives, matches latestReqId, is written to the cache and to items with resultsFor = 'iph'.
The live region says '8 suggestions' after 500 ms of quiet, so it does not chatter on every key.

flows.title: Choosing with the keyboard
steps: ArrowDown sets activeIndex 0; aria-activedescendant on the input points at option 0. DOM focus stays in the input.
Screen reader reads the option label and its position, for example '2 of 8'.
Enter calls onSelect(item), stores the query in recent searches, closes the list.
Escape instead closes the list and keeps the text; a second Escape clears it.

flows.title: Backspace from 'iphon' to 'ipho'
steps: The exact key is in the LRU cache, so items update in the next frame with no network.
If 'ipho' were missing but 'iph' was cached with complete=true, we filter the 'iph' items locally instead.

deepDives.title: When to fire: debounce, throttle, or neither
deepDives.problem: Firing on every key sends 8 requests for an 8-letter word, and most results are thrown away before they render. Waiting too long makes the box feel dead. The aim is the fewest requests that still make the list feel live.

options.name: Trailing debounce
options.how: Reset a 150–250 ms timer on each key; fetch when it expires.
pros: Fewest requests: fires only at pauses
Simple to reason about
cons: A fast, continuous typist sees nothing until they stop
Adds the full delay to every result

options.name: Throttle
options.how: Fetch at most once per 300 ms while typing, including the latest value at the end.
pros: Results keep updating during long typing
Upper bound on request rate
cons: Sends requests for prefixes the user will never look at
More responses to discard, so races matter more

options.name: Debounce with maxWait
options.how: Trailing debounce of 200 ms, but force a fetch if 600 ms pass without one.
pros: Pause behaviour of debounce, liveliness of throttle
Bounded staleness
cons: Two timers to test
Still delays every result by the wait

options.name: No delay, rely on cache and abort
options.how: Fetch on every key, abort the previous one, lean on CDN caching of short prefixes.
pros: Lowest perceived latency
Works well when the endpoint is cheap and edge-cached
cons: ~3× more requests
Aborted requests still cost the server if they already arrived

deepDives.choice: Debounce 200 ms with a 600 ms maxWait, and never fire while an IME composition is open (wait for compositionend). Cache hits skip the debounce entirely, since they cost nothing. If the backend were a cheap edge-cached index and the product team valued speed above cost, I would drop to 100 ms or fire on every key.

deepDives.title: Stale responses and race conditions
deepDives.problem: Requests for 'ip' and 'iph' are both in flight. 'ip' is slower, arrives last, and overwrites the list for 'iph'. The user now sees suggestions for the wrong text. Network order is not request order.

options.name: AbortController per request
options.how: Keep the current controller; call abort() before starting the next fetch.
pros: Frees the connection slot and saves bandwidth on slow links
fetch rejects with AbortError, which is easy to ignore
cons: Does not help if the response already resolved and is waiting in the microtask queue
Only works if the data source accepts a signal

options.name: Monotonic request id
options.how: Increment latestReqId on each fetch; when a response arrives, drop it unless its id equals latestReqId.
pros: Correct whatever the transport, even for a cache or worker source
Tiny and easy to test
cons: The losing request still runs to completion and uses bandwidth

options.name: Compare the response to the input
options.how: Server echoes q; render only if q equals the normalised current text.
pros: Guards against bugs elsewhere in the pipeline
cons: Breaks when two different texts normalise to the same key
Needs the server to echo the query

deepDives.choice: Use both abort and request id. Abort is the optimisation and the id check is the guarantee. Also keep resultsFor and only render items when it matches the visible text, so a bug elsewhere shows an old list dimmed, not a wrong one. In tests, use a fake fetch whose responses resolve in reverse order.

diagram.title: Out-of-order responses
diagram.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant C as Component
  participant S as Server
  U->>C: types ip
  C->>S: request 1 for ip
  U->>C: types iph
  C->>C: abort request 1
  C->>S: request 2 for iph
  S-->>C: response 2 for iph
  C->>C: id 2 is latest, render
  S-->>C: late response 1 for ip
  C->>C: id 1 is not latest, drop

deepDives.title: Caching by prefix
deepDives.problem: Users backspace, retype and search the same things. Each repeat over slow 4G costs ~190 ms. We want repeats to be instant and some new prefixes to need no request at all.

options.name: Exact-key LRU in memory
options.how: Map from normalised query to items, 100 entries, 5 minute TTL.
pros: Instant backspace
No staleness worries within a session
cons: Only exact repeats hit
Lost on reload

options.name: Narrow a complete parent result
options.how: If 'iph' returned complete=true (fewer than limit matches), filter those items locally for 'ipho' instead of fetching.
pros: Saves requests on long, specific queries
Zero latency
cons: Only correct if the server ranks by prefix match; fuzzy ranking breaks it
Needs the complete flag from the server

options.name: HTTP and CDN caching
options.how: Cache-Control: public, max-age=300 on the suggest endpoint; the CDN serves hot prefixes.
pros: Shared across all users; short prefixes are very hot
Browser HTTP cache survives reloads
cons: Cannot be personalised
Purging is coarse

options.name: Prefetch on focus
options.how: On focus, fetch suggestions for the empty query and preconnect to the API origin.
pros: Removes the 450 ms cold-connection cost
Popular items are ready for the first key
cons: Wasted calls for users who focus but never type

deepDives.choice: Exact-key LRU plus HTTP/CDN caching plus preconnect on focus. Add the 'narrow a complete parent' trick only if the server ranks by plain prefix, and gate it on the complete flag. If results were personalised, I would drop the shared CDN cache and keep only the in-memory one.

deepDives.title: Accessibility: combobox semantics and keyboard model
deepDives.problem: A div list under an input looks fine and is unusable for a screen-reader user. They don't know a list appeared, can't hear which option is active, and DOM focus moving into the list breaks typing.

options.name: aria-activedescendant
options.how: Input has role combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete list. DOM focus stays in the input; aria-activedescendant names the active option's id. Options have role option and aria-selected.
pros: User can keep typing at any time
One focus point, simple to manage
cons: Must scroll the active option into view yourself
Option ids must be unique and stable

options.name: Roving focus into the list
options.how: ArrowDown moves real DOM focus onto option elements.
pros: Native focus ring and scroll for free
cons: Typing a letter now goes to the option, not the input
Easy to lose focus when the list re-renders

options.name: Native datalist
options.how: Use input list= with a datalist element.
pros: Zero JavaScript, accessible by default
cons: No custom rendering, no thumbnails or groups
Inconsistent across browsers and on mobile

deepDives.choice: The ARIA 1.2 combobox with aria-activedescendant. Keyboard model: Down/Up move and wrap; Home/End stay with the input caret; Enter selects; Escape closes then clears; Tab closes without selecting. Add a polite live region that says how many results there are, updated after typing settles. Matched text uses <mark> built from ranges. Option rows are at least 44 px tall for touch. A datalist is fine for an internal tool that needs no custom rendering.

failures: Suggest API is down or returns 500
Keep the input fully working; show one quiet 'Suggestions unavailable' row; Enter still submits a normal search. Do not retry on every key: back off for 30 s.
Slow response arrives after the user has moved on
Request id check drops it; resultsFor guard keeps the list honest; abort frees the connection.
Korean or Japanese IME sends a request per jamo or kana
Ignore input events while composing; fetch on compositionend.
Labels are text nodes; highlight from ranges with <mark>; never use innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
localStorage throws (Safari private mode, storage full)
Wrap reads and writes in try/catch; recent searches simply don't show.
List opens and pushes the page down (CLS)
Render the popup absolutely positioned in a portal layer, with a fixed max height and its own scroll.
scale: 10× traffic: CDN caching of 1–3 character prefixes absorbs most of it; raise the client debounce slightly and add the complete-parent narrowing.
Large local data set (100 000+ items): build a prefix trie or sorted array once, in a Web Worker, and query it with the same request-id discipline.
Many products reuse it: extract a headless useCombobox hook (state, keyboard, ARIA props) and let teams supply rendering and data source.

followups.q: How would you test the race condition?
answer: Inject a fake fetchSuggestions that returns promises you resolve by hand.
Type 'ip' then 'iph', resolve 'iph' first, then 'ip'; assert the list still shows 'iph' results.
Use fake timers for the debounce, so the test is deterministic and fast.

followups.q: Should this be a controlled or uncontrolled component?
answer: Support both: value plus onQueryChange for parents that own the text, defaultValue for simple cases.
Keep the internal state (activeIndex, isOpen) private either way.
Warn in dev if a component switches between controlled and uncontrolled.
Use type=search and enterkeyhint=search for the right keyboard.
On small screens open a full-screen search sheet so the keyboard doesn't hide the list.
Bigger touch targets (44 px), and close the list on scroll start.

followups.q: How do you know it works in production?
answer: Track time from last keystroke to suggestions shown (p50/p95), split by connection type.
Suggestion click-through rate and the share of searches that come from a suggestion.
Count dropped stale responses and aborted requests to tune the debounce.

followups.q: What if the product wants inline ghost-text completion, like a code editor?
answer: That is aria-autocomplete='both': the top suggestion's remaining text is shown selected in the input.
Only complete when the top suggestion starts with exactly the typed text, or it feels broken.
Backspace must remove the ghost text, not the user's last character.

mistakes: Debouncing but forgetting the race: the slow old response still overwrites the new one.
Moving DOM focus into the list, so typing breaks and screen readers lose context.
Building highlighted labels with innerHTML from server strings.
Firing requests during IME composition, which floods the server for Korean and Japanese users.
Putting every keystroke in the URL and spamming browser history.

Named role combobox, role listbox, aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant
Handled loading, empty and error states
senior: Worked out that latency is round trips (warm ~190 ms vs cold ~640 ms) and proposed preconnect on focus
Designed a normalised cache key and an LRU, and explained when narrowing a parent result is safe
Rendered highlights from ranges, not HTML, and called out the XSS risk
Described the full keyboard model including Escape twice and Tab
